_meta.title: prompt, baked per pose by plan_qwen_frames

inputs.prompt: Image 2 is a coloured stick-figure pose skeleton. Draw the man from image 1 standing in that exact pose, at the same size and position in the frame as the skeleton, with empty background around him: his whole figure fits inside the frame, the whole of his afro, both shoes, both hands, both mallets and the whole marimba fully visible with margin on every side. seen in a three-quarter view from the side: the chest, hips, knees, toes and nose all point toward the lower right corner of the picture, the face in three-quarter view looking that way, playing out toward a crowd on that side, both feet flat on the floor, standing behind the marimba, leaning into a wide sweep, the arm on the left of the picture flung far out with its mallet, the other mallet down on a bar. He keeps his tall, narrow, long-armed adult build, long thin lined face, neatly trimmed short beard flecked with grey, round gold-rimmed spectacles, focused gentle smile, brown skin, big perfectly round black afro, long-sleeved cream dinner jacket buttoned closed, its narrow midnight-violet satin lapels lying flat on the chest, a small midnight-violet bow tie at a closed cream shirt collar, slim dark charcoal trousers and polished two-tone cream and dark shoes, and thick dark ink outline, behind a compact wooden marimba with a row of coral-red rosewood bars at his waist and a row of brass resonator tubes hanging beneath them, on a dark frame with two end legs, exactly as in image 1. Same pixel art style with crisp pixel clusters and cel shading. He has exactly two arms and two hands, each hand complete with fingers. He is a grown man of about forty. He holds two separate short mallets, one in each hand, each as long as his forearm with a round cream head. The marimba stands between him and the viewer at the same angle as his body, about as wide as he is tall and staying in the same place: its row of bars crosses in front of his belt and covers his hips, and its brass tubes hang in front of his thighs, with his shins and both shoes showing below them. The marimba is turned the same way: its row of bars runs on a diagonal, its end on the left of the picture nearer the viewer, larger and lower, and its end on the right of the picture smaller and higher. Do not draw the skeleton. Plain light grey background, full body.
